rows.en:
Hello, everyone.
This meeting is finally drawing to a close, isn't it?
...Though it seems the seventh person isn't going to show up.
Well, setting that aside, let me begin my story.
My name is Tomoharu Hosoda.
I'm a second-year.{p}

{a}{f:|}, you know that restroom beside the gym that's off-limits now, right?
That filthy restroom nobody can use, yet it's been left there all this time.
That restroom is creepy, isn't it?
It's a waste of space, too.
They should either fix it up and use it, or just tear it down...
But you see, there's a reason they can't fix it and can't tear it down.
Something shows up there.
No matter how many purifications they perform, no matter how important a person they call in, that one place is hopeless.{p}

Even I don't want to go near that one place.
The aura drifting there is one of a kind; its quality is different from anywhere else.
How should I put it... It isn't human.{p}Hey, {a}{f:|}, what do you think it is?
Foxes
Tanuki
Fish
Bugs

You got it right.
{a}{f:|}, have you maybe been near that place yourself?
You seem like the same type of person as me, {a}{f:|}.
If you got a strange feeling there, that's only natural.
So, the story about bugs.
Did you already know this story?
It's the reason that restroom stopped being used.{p}

A long time ago, there was a male student.
Unfortunately, I don't know his name.
He hated bugs with a passion.
But there are two kinds of hating, you know.
The type who hates something so much they don't want to go near it, and the type who hates something so much they kill it.
Which one are you, {a}{f:|}?
The type who stays away from things you hate?{p}Or the type who kills them?
The type who stays away
The type who kills them

Whoa, you're crueler than you look.
I'd better make sure you never come to hate me, ahahaha...
Anyway, he was the same way.
When he saw a bug, instead of running away, he'd chase it down and stomp it to death.{p}

I guess he was cruel to begin with.
Even bugs have souls, but I doubt he ever gave that a moment's thought.{p}

Back then, that restroom beside the gym could still be used normally.
Apparently everyone used it a lot after P.E. class.
And he used that restroom too.
Then he happened to look over and, what do you know, a house centipede was crawling along the restroom wall.
"Gross!"
He kicked the wall with his shoe and squashed that house centipede flat.
It was after that that he made a discovery.
That restroom, you see, maybe because it was so humid, was always damp, and full of bugs.{p}

House centipedes, centipedes, slugs... if you looked carefully, there were lots of bugs clinging to the floor and walls.
They say he spent most of his breaks in that restroom.
To kill bugs.
I think deep down he actually liked bugs.
Otherwise, I don't think he could have been so obsessed with them.
They say he practically lived in that restroom, as if something had possessed him.
It was a real obsession.
Apparently he used to say it all the time.{p}

"I'll kill every last bug in this world!"
Just like that.
Scary, isn't it?
I'm pretty fond of bugs, so it gives me the chills.{p}

Eventually, just killing bugs wasn't enough for him anymore.
Until then, he'd been satisfied just squashing them, but no matter how long he kept at it, the number of bugs never went down.
A day later, they'd gather in that restroom again from who knows where.
Well, of course they would.
There's no end of bugs, after all.
Him trying hard all by himself was a truly wasted effort.
So he thought about it.
Why did the bugs keep gathering?{p}

Bugs must have at least a little intelligence.
So if their companions were killed more cruelly, even bugs would get scared and stay away from here.
That's what he thought.
Quite an idea, isn't it?
If it were me, I'd think of some other way.
Like improving the ventilation, or keeping the restroom cleaner.
That would be more constructive, right?
But he was different.
And he carried it out, exactly as he'd planned.
Mostly for his own satisfaction.{p}

Tearing the legs and bodies off house centipedes and centipedes was a given.
He burned them with matches, poured strange liquids on them, stabbed them with thumbtacks and needles...
That restroom became something like a torture chamber for bugs.
Even his friends finally told him to stop, but he wouldn't listen to a word.
And he began to study even crueler ways of killing them.{p}

But the bugs didn't decrease one bit.
As if mocking his efforts, far from decreasing, they increased.
Like soldiers on a battlefield, climbing over the corpses of their fallen comrades to fight on.
He fought.
All alone, against the tiny bugs...{p}

"Let's try this method next."
He used cellophane tape to stick lots of bugs onto a big stone, about the size of a pickling stone.
So they couldn't move.
Then he'd slam it down onto the ground.
The bugs got sandwiched between the big stone and the concrete and squashed with a splat.
"How do you like that!
Did you see that, you lot?
That's how I'll kill bugs like you!
Hurry up and vanish from this world!"
He screamed it.
At an invisible enemy.{p}

But the bugs heard those words.
All kinds of bugs were clinging thickly to the restroom windows, listening intently to what he said.
And as if defying his words, the bugs multiplied more and more.
The way they multiplied wasn't normal.
The boys' restroom and the girls' restroom were both hit.{p}

You'd go to the restroom, and suddenly something would drip, drip down onto your hair from above.
You'd reach up to brush it off, and a giant centipede would coil around your fingers...
...You'd look up, and the ceiling would be covered with centipedes.
Or the water in the sinks would suddenly clog.
You'd look, and find the drain stuffed with dead bugs.
Things like that kept happening one after another.
The girls, apparently, made a huge fuss.
They stormed into the faculty room shouting that they'd never, ever use that restroom again.
And after that, hardly anyone used that restroom anymore.{p}

Of course, the boy who kept killing bugs got called in by the teachers too.
Apparently they chewed him out pretty badly.
Even so, he didn't learn his lesson at all.
He blamed the bugs, saying it was all their fault he got called in and scolded by the teachers.
He became even more determined to fight.
Once it gets that far, it's just abnormal, isn't it?
And then he resorted to one final measure.{p}What do you think he did?
He tried to find the bugs' boss
He tried to burn the restroom
I can't even imagine

"...Making a fool of me.
...I'll kill you!
...Every last one of you, I'll kill you all!"
He kept muttering things like that, over and over.
The school at night is very dark.
That restroom especially, since its fluorescent light was broken.
It was dim even in the daytime.
At night, you couldn't see a thing.
As he got close to the restroom, what do you know, there was a rustling sound.
A rustling, scraping sound, like things rubbing their bodies together, was coming from the restroom.
He held his breath and stepped into the restroom.
And then... it felt different under his feet than usual.{p}

There was no hard floor; the footing felt somehow unsteady and squishy.
When he pressed down and put his weight on his foot, it felt like stepping on a thick, fluffy carpet.{p}

Under the squishy stuff, he could feel the hard floor.
Without thinking, he shone the flashlight he was holding onto the floor.{p}

And the inside of the restroom was packed with every kind of bug imaginable.
And not just the floor, either, but the walls and the ceiling too.
It was less a restroom than the inside of the stomach of some unknown creature.
The floor, the walls, the ceiling, all of it was rustling and writhing as if it were alive itself.
For the first time, he felt afraid.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

He froze in place.
He felt as if he finally understood how terrifying the enemy he'd been trying to fight really was.
This was not an enemy he could ever fight.
The bugs are mighty...
That thought kept spinning around in his head.
But even though his mind was thinking that, his body wouldn't obey him.
He was so terrified that he acted on reflex.{p}

The person who found him the next day was left speechless.
The restroom reeked so much of gasoline that they went to look, and what do you know, there were huge numbers of dead bugs.{p}

Dead bugs were piled up like mountains on the floor, so there was nowhere to set foot.
Among them was one spot heaped especially high, like a little hill.
When they dug through it, a human face came out.
It was him.
He must have been terrified, because his hair had turned pure white, and he was all dried up like a mummy, as if all the life had drained out of his body.{p}

...What's wrong?
Are you feeling sick?
Your face has gone pale.
Should I stop the story here?{p}Or do you want to hear a little more?
I want you to stop
I'll hear a little more

Are you sure you're okay?
If you hate bugs, I can stop.
Are you really okay?
...All right, then I'll go on.{p}

After that incident, the restroom couldn't be used anymore.
Even when they cleared away the dead bugs, more bugs would gather from out of nowhere.
Besides, even if the bugs were gone, nobody would want to use a restroom like that, right?
These days hardly anyone knows this story, so it's fine, but back then everyone knew it.
Since nobody used it anymore, the only option left was to tear it down.
So they called in contractors to demolish the restroom, and... bad things happened.
Everyone involved in the work, you see, was tormented by nightmares.
Apparently it was a dream of having their bodies eaten by swarms of bugs.
If it were just one night, it would only be a bad dream, but it went on for days.
And it happened to every single person involved.
They all became afraid to sleep, and on top of that, couldn't stand the sight of bugs anymore.
So the work was called off.
And that restroom is still there today.
...Though it seems bugs don't show up in that restroom anymore these days.{p}

Well, that story is just a rumor passed down at this school.
Nobody actually saw it, and nobody checked it, either.
I'm just repeating what I heard from an upperclassman, word for word.
So it's not very credible, is it?{p}Would you believe that story, if it were you?
I believe it
I don't believe it
Maybe it could be true

Right?
If you don't see it with your own eyes, you can't believe a gross story like that.
I was the same way.
I was just like you, {a}{f:|}.{p}

...Actually, a friend of mine fell victim to it.
All because he used that restroom.
That friend's name was Keiichi Tsuda.
Tsuda didn't use that restroom for fun or anything.
He knew the stories about that restroom, more or less.
And he hated bugs, too.
In Tsuda's case, though, hating bugs meant he was the type to run away.
Far from killing bugs, he was the type who couldn't even go near them.
So there's no way he'd ever go to a restroom with rumors like that by choice.{p}

Even so, one day, after P.E. class, he suddenly had to go to the restroom.
It was better than wetting himself, so he went, reluctantly.{p}

...Luckily, there were no bugs.
Even so, the walls were covered in dark, blackish stains.
He knew right away that they were stains from squashed bugs.
So he tried his hardest not to look, not to look, and hurried to do his business.
He held his breath, shut his eyes, and thought only about getting out of the restroom.
And when he was done, he made a dash for it.{p}

Outside the restroom was a whole different world.
Then, just as he stretched out big and took a deep breath...{p}

"Aagh!"
Tsuda couldn't help screaming.
He looked, and there was a huge spider on his shoulder.
It was a big joro spider with a yellow-and-black striped abdomen.
Thinking it must have hitched a ride when he went to the restroom, he jumped up and shook his whole body.{p}

The joro spider fell from his shoulder and scuttled away just like that.
Even so, Tsuda's heart was still pounding.
And he got worried that there might be other bugs on him besides that one.
But he couldn't search.
He was too scared.
That's how people who hate bugs are.
What if there's one on my back? What if there's one on my head?
Even while thinking that, he was too scared to check.
His body froze up, you see.
That's how much he hated bugs, and how scared of them he was.
And he swore he would never go near that restroom again.{p}

Then one day, a few days later.
It was during lunch break.{p}

I'd finished my lunch and gone up to the roof, and over in a corner, Tsuda was eating his lunch alone.
Tsuda was a light eater.
He always ate like the food tasted awful.
As for me, mealtime is when I'm happiest.
Tsuda was the exact opposite.
He always seemed to be forcing himself to eat because he had to.{p}

But get this.
That time, he was wolfing it down like a different person.
He was shoveling the contents of his lunch box into his mouth at a furious pace.
I waved and walked over to him.
"Hey, Tsuda!"
Tsuda only gave me a quick glance and didn't stop his chopsticks for a second.
He had to be eating something really tasty.
Thinking maybe I'd ask him for a bite too, I went closer, and...
I nearly threw up what I'd just eaten.{p}

Then, once he'd polished off a whole lunch box of flies, he wiped his mouth, looking very satisfied, and let out a sigh.
And then he looked at me.
"What's wrong, Hosoda?"
He said it as if he couldn't understand why I was standing there frozen.
Then he closed the lid of his lunch box, walked right past me, and went downstairs.{p}

I couldn't move for a while.
Even now, I can't forget the way he looked at me.
That wasn't the way you look at a friend.
No, it was nothing that mild.
That wasn't the way you look at a human being.
It was the way you look at food.
After that, I decided to keep away from Tsuda.
I mean, wouldn't you?
Even if it was just an illusion I saw, I didn't want to be looked at with those eyes.
But bad luck comes looking for you anyway.
During chemistry class, I was told to go and fetch some lab equipment.
The teacher picked me by name.{p}

"Hosoda, Tsuda, sorry, but could you go to the prep room and bring back the equipment?"
Hey, {a}{f:|}, what would you do?{p}Would you want to be alone with a guy who eats flies like they're delicious?
Go with him
Ask the teacher to pick someone else

I begged the teacher desperately.
I said I had a headache, a stomachache, whatever, and escaped to the nurse's office.
The teacher looked annoyed, but let me go.
No matter what, I didn't want to be alone with Tsuda.
But that was a mistake.{p}

There was no one in the nurse's office.
I was lying in bed by myself.
Then, after a while, I heard a noise over by the door.
Thinking the school nurse had come back, I looked over, and...{p}

Tsuda was standing there.
With that look in his eyes, like he was looking at food.
Without thinking, I murmured,
"...Tsuda."
Tsuda was smiling.
It was the smile of someone who had cornered his prey.
"...Hosoda, that's mean of you.
Do you hate me or something?
I've had that feeling these past few days."
Then he slowly came toward the bed.{p}

I couldn't move.
I was paralyzed.
I was so terrified that my whole body had seized up.
Just like a bug caught in a spider's web.
Tsuda seemed to know that too.
He wasn't in any hurry; he came closer slowly, ever so slowly.
"...Hosoda, you're nice and fat, you look delicious.
What kind of things do you eat to get like that?"
As he said that, he suddenly climbed up onto my bed.
He straddled me and drooled happily.{p}

I wanted to cry.
And I knew for certain this was the end.
Fangs had grown in Tsuda's mouth.
And strands were trailing from his gaping mouth.
Not drool, but real silk.
He was just like a spider.
He's going to eat me!
...Just as I thought that, my body moved, just a little.
It was truly a godsend.
Somehow I managed to twist my body just a little.{p}

"Aagh!"
It happened all of a sudden.
All I did was twist my body, but out of nowhere Tsuda started writhing in agony.
He tumbled off the bed, clutching his head and kicking his legs wildly.
My paralysis broke, you see.
Without thinking, I threw off the blanket that was on top of me.
And then...
Under my body, a joro spider had been crushed flat.
Its abdomen had burst, and a thick, gooey fluid was oozing out.
And Tsuda stopped moving right there.
I ran.
I left Tsuda lying there.{p}

When I came to, I was in a hospital bed.
I'd been saved.
And I savored the joy of being alive with my whole body.
"Hosoda."
Suddenly, I heard someone calling my name.
Puzzled, I turned toward the voice, and...{p}

It was Tsuda.
Tsuda was lying in the bed next to mine.
The shock I felt then, I can't even put into words.
My heart really nearly stopped.{p}What do you think I did then?
Fight Tsuda
Stay still
Call the nurse for help

"...What's wrong, Hosoda?
I never thought you'd end up in the hospital too.
But it's nice that our beds are right next to each other, huh?"
He said that and smiled.
He seemed somehow different from the Tsuda of a moment ago.
So I worked up my nerve and asked him.{p}

"...Hey, Tsuda.
Do you ever feel like you want to eat me?"
Tsuda just stared at me blankly.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Ah ha ha ha...
What are you saying, Hosoda?
Have you gone crazy or something?"
The Tsuda laughing in front of me was the usual Tsuda.
He didn't have that look.
I was so relieved I let out a long sigh.
And then Tsuda suddenly turned serious and said this.{p}

rows.en:
"...You know, I can't remember the last few days.
I wonder what happened to me.
I went to that restroom beside the gym, and a joro spider got on my shoulder there...
After that, I don't remember a thing.
And when I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.
Weird, right?"
As if his words were prompting me, I found myself nodding.
And I kept what I'd seen on the roof and what happened in the nurse's office to myself.
I mean, I didn't think Tsuda would believe me if I told him all that.{p}

I think Tsuda was probably being controlled by the joro spider.
Of course, I didn't tell him that either.
Well, Tsuda was back to normal, after all.
Case closed, as they say.
Tsuda still comes to school like normal, even now.
He's doing just fine.
It's just that sometimes, when he sees a fly, he gets that look in his eyes and licks his lips like it looks delicious.
And sometimes when Tsuda opens his mouth wide to laugh, thread comes spewing out of it...
But I'm not scared anymore.
That sort of thing is just a minor aftereffect.
In exchange, Tsuda now wolfs down everything like it's delicious, and he isn't scared of bugs anymore either.{p}
So, what do you think, {a}{f:|}?{p}Now will you believe the story about that restroom?
I believe it
I don't believe it
I might believe it if I met Tsuda

...You're a suspicious one, aren't you?
All right.
Then I'll bring him along sometime.
But I think you'd better believe in the curse of the bugs, at least.
If you keep killing things just because they're bugs, you'll be cursed for sure.
Bugs are alive too, you know.
At least remember that much for me.{p}

...And that's the end of my story.
...The seventh person still hasn't come, huh.
That means the next one is finally the last.
{a}{f:|}, I hope nothing happens.
...Because I think you're starting to notice it too.
The eerie aura that's enveloping this room.{p}

I see, that's nice.
Usually, if you don't go near them, they shouldn't do anything to you either.
That's the most peaceful way, isn't it?
I wish everyone were like that.
There are lots of people in this world who aren't satisfied unless they kill.
The guy I'm about to tell you about was exactly like that.
He was the type who, when he saw a bug, would chase it until he'd killed it.{p}

He tried to find the boss of the bugs, you see.
He'd decided all on his own that this mass outbreak of bugs was happening because some bug ringleader was giving the orders.{p}

One day after school, he went to that restroom to find the boss of the bugs.
And he took a stick and stirred it all around the restroom, where bugs were swarming in huge numbers.{p}

Bugs came welling up, as if overflowing, out of the toilets, the cleaning closet and the sinks.
Gradually the sun went down, and he turned on the restroom light and kept on searching.
The place felt less like a restroom than the inside of some unknown creature's stomach.
The floor, the walls and the ceiling were all rustling and squirming, as if they themselves were alive.
For the first time, he felt fear.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

rows.en:
He stood frozen.
He felt he finally understood how truly frightening the enemy he'd been trying to fight was.
But having come this far, he couldn't back down a single step.
By then he was half doing it out of sheer stubbornness.
"Wh-where's the boss of these things☆"
Unable to take it anymore, he shouted.{p}

rows.en: Saying that, he swatted the moth out of the air with his stick as it flew at his face.{p}

From the shock of the blow, the moth fell to the floor with a splat, scattering its scales.
The moth's plump, swollen belly was cruelly crushed, splattering yellow guts everywhere.
For a while, the moth's wings kept twitching and jerking.
Watching it, he basked in a sense of triumph, thinking he'd defeated the boss of this place.
In the dim restroom light, the moth's scales glittered.
The scales drifted down like falling snow.
Just then, he realized his body was slowly going numb.
"...Damn, it's those scales★"
Before he could even finish saying it, he collapsed.
His vision slowly went dark, and his consciousness faded away...{p}
As his consciousness faded, all he could faintly make out in front of him was the crushed moth.{p}

They say he was found about three days after he died.
The cause of death was supposedly that he'd slipped in the restroom, fallen and hit his head in a bad spot.
But they say his body was in an incredible state.
Apparently...
From inside his half-rotted mouth, moth after moth that had emerged from its cocoon was flapping its wings open.
Circling round and round over his face, as if they were dancing.{p}

You can't imagine, right?
I mean, you can tell a guy like that isn't normal.
Normal people like us could never figure him out.
He tried to smoke those bugs to death, you see.
With mosquito coils.
{a}{f:|}, don't laugh.
People die from getting caught in the smoke in fires too, right?
It's the same with bugs.
He wasn't going to kill them all in one go.
He chose a way that would make the bugs die slowly, in agony.{p}

He took mosquito coils and marched into the school in the middle of the night.
"...Making a fool of me.
...I'll kill you!
...Every last one of you, I'll wipe you all out!"
He kept muttering things like that, over and over.
The school at night is very dark.
And the fluorescent light in that restroom was broken, too.
It was dim even in the daytime.
At night, you couldn't see a thing.
As he got close to the restroom, he heard a rustling noise.
A scratchy, scraping sound, like things rubbing their bodies together, was coming from the restroom.
He left only the one exit he'd use to get out at the end, and sealed all the other windows from the outside with duct tape.
So the smoke couldn't escape.{p}
Holding his breath, he stepped into the restroom.{p}

Under the squishy stuff, he could feel the hard floor.
Without thinking, he shone the flashlight he was holding onto the floor.{p}

And the inside of the restroom was packed with every kind of bug imaginable.
And not just the floor, either, but the walls and the ceiling too.
It was less a restroom than the inside of the stomach of some unknown creature.
The floor, the walls, the ceiling, all of it was rustling and writhing as if it were alive itself.
For the first time, he felt afraid.
The bugs had been waiting, you see.
Waiting for him to come.{p}

He stood frozen.
He felt he finally understood how truly frightening the enemy he'd been trying to fight was.
But having come this far, he couldn't back down a single step.
By then he was half doing it out of sheer stubbornness.{p}

rows.en:
He bundled twenty mosquito coils together and lit them all at once with a lighter.
In the darkness, the lighter's flame lit him up red.
The coils caught, and smoke filled the air around him.
He scattered them all over the restroom and tried to get outside himself.
But the floor was slick with the body fluids of the bugs he'd trampled, and he couldn't walk properly.
He heard the bugs, reacting to the smoke from the coils, rustling as if they were writhing in agony.
It was a rustling like they were putting a curse on him.{p}

"Waaaaaah!"
Terrified, he screamed.
He struggled desperately to escape.
And then he realized.
The reason he couldn't move was that the bugs had caught hold of his legs...{p}

His legs were already buried in bugs up to about the thighs.
Unable to even move anymore, he was swallowed up by the bugs.
The next day, the person who found him was left speechless.
Duct tape was stuck all over the restroom, and it smelled kind of like incense, so they thought something was strange.{p}

"{f:Stop it|Please stop}!"
{f:I|I} was half shouting it.
I felt so sick I couldn't stand it{f:|}.
"Fine, I'm happy to stop here, you know.
{a}{f:|}, you must never use that restroom, no matter what...
I can't promise you'll be safe."
Hosoda said that and looked at {f:me|me}.
For an instant, {f:I|I} couldn't move.
Because on Hosoda's shoulder was a yellow-and-black striped... yes, that was a joro spider{f:|}.
There was a joro spider right there on Hosoda's shoulder{f:!|!}{p}

"Oh, this guy?"
With that, Hosoda let the joro spider out the window.
"Haven't you ever heard?
Spiders hold grudges.
My grandma always used to tell me that bad things happen if you kill one."
Hosoda went back to his seat.
"Well then, who's next?"{p}

Really?
You believe me, then.
That makes me happy.
I believe it myself, too.{p}

I really didn't want to.
But the teacher had called me by name, so I couldn't exactly say "I can't go with this person."
Not with him standing right there, either...
The two of us walked down the hallway awkwardly...
I prayed to God.
Please don't let him start saying anything weird...{p}

"...Hosoda, haven't you been avoiding me lately?
Do you hate me?"
Tsuda muttered it to me quietly.
Honestly, I never should have made that prayer to God.
"Huh? No, of course not.
What's this silly stuff you're saying?
Let's hurry up and get to the prep room."
I said it in a fluster.{p}

The prep room is full of all sorts of equipment.
The room is really cramped.
We'd been asked to bring back tripods, alcohol lamps and asbestos pads.
I quickly loaded the equipment onto a tray and tried to leave the prep room.
I felt I had to get out of that closed-in room even a second sooner.{p}

Then I saw Tsuda standing in the doorway, staring at me.
It seemed he'd been following my every move with his eyes the whole time.
With that look of his, like he was looking at food.
I backed away without thinking.
"I knew it.
What you said earlier was a lie, wasn't it?
You really are avoiding me."
Tsuda said that without taking his eyes off me.{p}

And then he reached behind him and shut the prep room door.
"...I'm so lonely.
And here I am, so fond of you.
I mean, you look so delicious.
Let's see... those pink cheeks of yours, for one."{p}

Tsuda was smiling.
On reflex, I tried to light an alcohol lamp.
...But it seemed I'd forgotten to put matches on the tray, and I couldn't light it.
It's over... Am I going to become his food too, like those bugs...?
The moment I thought that, I heard a voice from outside.
"Hey, they said they want the other equipment brought over too."
It was a classmate.
I was saved!
I hurried to answer.
"I-I'm opening the door right now!"
I heard Tsuda click his tongue.
Somehow, I'd escaped.{p}

...After that, Tsuda stopped acting strangely.
He never attacked me again, and he never ate bugs again either.
But it seems he's still after me even now.
Sometimes he stares at me with a slimy, clinging look.
I'm sure he's trying to get me to let my guard down so he can make his move the moment he sees an opening.{p}

...{a}{f:|}.
If one day I suddenly stop coming to school...
you can be sure Tsuda had a hand in it.
When that happens, please, look into him.
And I want you to save me.
I'm begging you...
That's the end of my story.
Well then, shall we hear the next person's story...{p}

On reflex, I lunged at Tsuda.
I sat on top of him and choked him.
And what do you know, joro spiders came swarming out of his mouth.
I let go of his neck, shoved my hand into his mouth and made him throw up everything in his stomach.
"Urgh. Urghhhh!"
Mixed in with the contents of his stomach, a whole bunch of joro spiders came out, squirming.
And before those spiders could get away, I beat them to death with a slipper.
I still can't forget how that felt.
All the strength drained out of my body.
I'd killed the joro spiders, but I was worried about him, so I called out to him.
"Tsuda... Tsuda?"
He was coughing and hacking.
Maybe I'd gone a little too far just now.
But if I hadn't gone that far, who knows what would've happened to him... That's what I told myself.{p}

Tsuda turned to look at me.
He'd been choking, so there were tears running down his face.
Seeing him like that, I worked up my nerve and asked him.
"...Hey, Tsuda.
Do you ever feel like you want to eat me?"
Tsuda just stared at me blankly.
Then he burst out laughing.
"Ah ha ha ha...
What are you saying, Hosoda?
Have you gone crazy or something?"
The Tsuda laughing in front of me was the usual Tsuda.
He didn't have that look.
I was so relieved I let out a long sigh.{p}

rows.en:
I went to that restroom beside the gym, and a joro spider got on my shoulder there...
After that, I don't remember a thing.
And when I came to, I was lying in a hospital bed.
Weird, right?"{p}

As if his words were prompting me, I found myself nodding.
"But hey, this mess around the bed... did I throw up or something?
That's so embarrassing, geez..."
He laughed cheerfully.
He really didn't seem to remember anything at all.{p}
I called the nurse for help.{p}

At the top of my lungs.
The nurse came running right away.
Thinking about it now, I should've just used the nurse call button.
But at the time, I couldn't think of anything like that.
"What's wrong★"
I told the nurse everything that had happened.
Of course there was no way the nurse would believe me... not a ridiculous story like that...
I got a shot of tranquilizer.{p}

I don't know how long I slept, but when I woke up, Tsuda was no longer in the bed next to mine.
It seemed to be night, but it wasn't lights-out yet.
Which meant it was still before nine...
I was thinking things like that when I happened to look up at the ceiling.{p}

"★"
I strained my eyes and looked again.
I was sure that just now, a joro spider had been up there...
I spent the whole night without sleeping a wink.{p}

The next day, Tsuda came to visit me.
"Hosoda, are you all right?"
He said it looking worried about me.
I couldn't even look him straight in the eye.
...An awkward silence hung between us.
I worked up my nerve and asked him.{p}

...I see.
Thank you.
You believe me.
If it were a story I'd heard secondhand, you might not be able to believe it, but I experienced it myself, after all.{p}

Oh yeah, ever since then, Tsuda has had this weird mark on him.
He says it won't go away.
...It's shaped like a tiny spider, about the size of the tip of your pinkie.
Next time I'll bring him along and show you that mark.
Apparently, every month that mark moves to a different spot on his body.
I wonder if that's an aftereffect too.
Or else...
No, it's fine. I got rid of that spider back then, after all...
...And that's the end of my story.
Still, the seventh person sure is late.
Well, there's no point waiting forever.
If they still haven't come after the next story, let's just go home.{p}

I mean, you don't believe it, right?
I'll wait for you outside the restroom.
If anything happens, I'll come save you.
After all, experiencing it yourself is the best way to believe something.
Okay, {a}{f:|}?
It's a promise.
Well then, shall we hear the next story...{p}

Too bad.
The answer was a fox.
Well, to people like us, tanuki and foxes are pretty much the same thing, right?
Anyway, about why that restroom stopped being used.{p}

Once, there was a boy at this school.
Unfortunately, I don't know his name.
He had a strong sixth sense too.
Apparently, in his own self-taught way, he'd look at everyone with what he called "spirit vision."
He loved fortune-telling, too.
There were always students crowded around him, wanting their fortunes told.{p}{a}{f:|}, would you want him to tell your fortune too?
I'd want my fortune told
I don't need my fortune told

{a}{f:|}, you know about Kokkuri-san, right?
Yeah, that thing where you draw a torii gate and letters and tell fortunes with a coin.
He was especially good at Kokkuri-san, you see.
And apparently his Kokkuri-san fortunes were often right.
But it's a dangerous thing, calling up spirits to tell fortunes.
To put it bluntly, it's low-level spirits that come down.
There's no way a high-level spirit would come down.
In the end, the only things that answer impure human wishes like that are low-level spirits trying to slip into the cracks in people's hearts...
And everyone does it half for fun. They've sure got some nerve, don't they?
Even my cousin did Kokkuri-san half for fun, and the spirit wouldn't leave.{p}

My cousin's family owned a small factory, but a little while after that it was driven into bankruptcy, and an employee in despair hanged themselves in the factory.
My cousin's grandpa went on the first shrine visit of the New Year and died when the crowd toppled like dominoes on the shrine steps.
And my cousin came down with some rare disease and died, just like that.
All of this happened within three years of my cousin doing Kokkuri-san.
No, sure, it might just be a coincidence.
But it's way too scary a story to write off as coincidence, isn't it?{p}

Back to the earlier story.
About that guy who was good at fortune-telling.
He went crazy too, you see.
The story goes that in his case, too, Kokkuri-san wouldn't leave.
They say he was like someone possessed.
He still came to school, but apparently he hardly ever went to class.{p}

And they say he often went to that restroom.
Maybe nobody was especially interested in him, but no one knew what he was doing in there.
A teacher apparently saw it: he'd drawn Kokkuri-san letter boards all over the restroom walls.
And he was laughing, holding a ten-yen coin.
Well, the way it ends is that he hanged himself in there.
The story goes that even now, a ten-yen coin sometimes appears out of nowhere and glides across the letter board on that wall.{p}

Still, that alone isn't very convincing, is it?
After all, I'm just repeating a story I heard from an upperclassman, word for word.
But you know, there's more to this story.{p}{a}{f:|}, are you interested in the rest of it?
I'm interested
Not really
All right, I'll tell you.{p}
